StableRonaldo sparks controversy after pointing gun on IRL stream
item.description: Popular streamer StableRonaldo sparked outrage after a clip showed him pointing a handgun at another car in Los Angeles during a live stream. He claimed he felt followed. Viewers debated if the weapon was real, but displaying any firearm, even a replica, in public can lead to serious legal trouble in California, highlighting the dangers of IRL streaming.
item.dc:creator: Sumit Roy

item.title: 99% of jobs could vanish by 2027 – only 5 types may survive, warns AI expert
item.description: AI researcher Dr. Roman Yampolskiy warns that artificial general intelligence could automate nearly all jobs by 2027, driving unprecedented unemployment. Unlike past revolutions, few human roles would remain, limited to oversight, AI intermediaries, counseling, or niche human-made crafts. He predicts society may reach a technological singularity by 2045, where AI progress outpaces human comprehension, fundamentally challenging the relevance of human labor.

item.title: ‘America’s elections are rigged, stolen’: Trump renews claims, warns US must fix system or lose country
item.description: Former President Donald Trump is once again asserting that American elections are rigged, demanding sweeping reforms like mandatory photo ID and proof of citizenship to restore trust. He proposes limiting mail-in voting, framing these as crucial for the nation's survival.

item.title: Queen Elizabeth's response to Prince Andrew's Epstein links revealed: 'Full support from mum'
item.description: Freshly unveiled documents related to Epstein shed light on Queen Elizabeth's delicate perspective regarding Prince Andrew's connection to the financier. Though her spokesperson emphasized her 'complete support' for Andrew, the Queen reportedly expressed privately that his ongoing interactions with Epstein were 'ill-advised.' This revelation surfaced against the backdrop of ongoing examinations into images featuring Andrew alongside Epstein and Virginia Giuffre.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Did everything right, still failed’: Indian student plans to leave US after job hunt stalls
item.description: A 27-year-old Indian man, after completing a Master's degree in the US, is returning to India due to an inability to secure employment. Despite aggressively applying for jobs daily, he faced rejections citing visa status and sponsorship needs, a situation exacerbated by new H-1B petition fees.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Mizkif-linked Twitch account receives temporary suspension
item.description: Popular streamer Mizkif's secondary Twitch account received a 24-hour suspension for promoting a competitor in the stream title. Twitch enforces strict rules against using its platform's discovery features to direct viewers elsewhere, even for minor violations on non-main accounts. The brief suspension served as a reminder of Twitch's policies on platform promotion.
item.dc:creator: Sumit Roy

item.title: Streamer Kyedae confirms breakup with TenZ, ending six-year relationship
item.description: Popular Twitch streamer Kyedae Shymko has announced her breakup with VALORANT personality TenZ after six years together. The couple, who started dating at 17, mutually decided to part ways due to growing apart and a need for individual growth, not a specific conflict. Their separation, hinted at by social media changes, brings closure to fans.
item.dc:creator: Sumit Roy

item.title: Did ancient Egypt record biblical giants? A 3,300-year-old text raises new questions
item.description: A 3,300-year-old Egyptian papyrus held by the British Museum has reignited debate over whether biblical references to giants reflect historical encounters or myth. The Anastasi I manuscript describes unusually tall Shosu people, drawing interest from faith-based researchers while historians urge caution, noting the text’s likely satirical nature and the lack of archaeological evidence supporting the existence of ancient giants.
item.dc:creator: TOI Trending Desk

item.title: Colder than Antarctica? What caused New York’s life-threatening deep freeze
item.description: New York City experienced temperatures colder than parts of Antarctica on Sunday, with wind chills reaching 14 degrees below zero. This extreme cold, driven by Arctic air, prompted rare warnings for millions. The prolonged deep freeze marks the most extreme in at least a decade for many Northeast locations.

item.title: Two Indian American men indicted for allegedly using 3,000 stolen identities to defraud online gambling sites of $3 million
item.description: Two Indian American men from Glastonbury face federal charges for allegedly using thousands of stolen identities to defraud online gambling platforms, including FanDuel, of approximately $3 million. Amitoj Kapoor and Siddharth Lillaney are accused of exploiting new user incentives with illicitly obtained personal data, leading to charges of fraud, identity theft, and money laundering.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Nobel Peace Prize winner Narges Mohammadi sentenced to fresh jail term in Iran
item.description: Nobel laureate Narges Mohammadi has received over seven additional years in prison, alongside a two-year travel ban and internal exile, according to her lawyer. The Iranian activist, already incarcerated, is reportedly on a hunger strike. This latest sentence follows her persistent campaigning against the regime's human rights abuses, including the death penalty and mandatory dress codes.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Japan snap elections: PM Sanae Takaichi’s LDP secures majority in lower house
item.description: Japan's ruling LDP, led by PM Sanae Takaichi, is poised for a significant win in snap elections, exit polls suggest. This victory could empower Takaichi to advance her conservative agenda, including increased defense spending. However, voter concerns about inflation and economic stability persist, alongside heightened regional tensions with China.

item.title: ‘She nearly died’: 18-month-old girl was returned to ICE custody, denied medication despite life-threatening illness, lawsuit says
item.description: An 18-month-old girl, Amalia, was hospitalized with a life-threatening respiratory illness while detained by US immigration authorities. She was returned to custody and denied medication after her release from the hospital, amidst a measles outbreak at the Dilley, Texas facility. Her parents, also detained, sued for their release.
